issues.description: StockIngredient exposes its quantity via different getter names across artifacts: the template defines retrieveQuantity(), while the solution (and typical getter naming implied by the requirement to "add getters for all private fields") provides getQuantity(). This inconsistent API name can confuse students and breaks any starter/usage code that expects getQuantity() in the template context.
issues.suggestedFix: In the template StockIngredient, rename retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity(), or add a getQuantity() method that returns quantity (optionally keeping retrieveQuantity() as a delegating alias). Ensure any template code uses the chosen getter consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement is internally inconsistent about whether SealSaloon.stock is static: the UML association depicts stock as an instance relationship, but later text explicitly requires the stock attribute (and related methods) to be static/shared across all saloon instances. Students following the diagram may implement a non-static stock, conflicting with the textual requirement and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the UML consistent with the text by marking stock as a static attribute (e.g., showing it as +{static} stock: Stock or an explicit static field in the class box) and/or adjusting the association notation to indicate static/shared. Keep the diagram and the written requirement aligned with the intended tests.
